set.body:
Source: 2026-08-03 codec field audit (the A7 follow-up review).

Problem: JobRef deliberately dropped cluster identity, and both hand-written decoders discarded any `cluster` they found. But both first ran ClusterName.from on it and propagated the failure: AgentDomainJson.decodeRemoteJobRef and StructuredJson.decodeJob. No encoder has ever written the field, so this could only affect a legacy or foreign payload, which is exactly the compatibility path where a spurious rejection costs most. StructuredJson.decodeJob feeds the durable result envelope, handle and invocation decoders, so a stored record carrying a cluster string that failed validation became unreadable over a value nothing would have used.

Fix: ignore the field outright at both sites rather than validating it.

Evidence: RED first. A test decoding a job reference whose cluster is "not a valid cluster name!" failed before the change and passes after.
set.title: P8.A14: Stop validating a legacy cluster field that JobRef discards
